title: Build stronger Tribal broadband programs with better grant, contract, and project controls
summary: Tribal governments and organizations are making significant investments in broadband infrastructure to expand access to education, healthcare, employment, public safety and other essential services. New and continuing funding opportunities—including the Tribal Broadband Connectivity Program (TBCP), California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) programs and other federal and state initiatives—can help advance these priorities.

title: Modernizing and consolidating an enterprise EHR
summary: A regional, not-for-profit health system in the Midwest with more than 8,000 employees, serving patients across a multi-state area through multiple hospitals and hundreds of care locations. Following the acquisition of four hospitals and numerous physician clinics, the health system needed to rapidly modernize and consolidate its electronic health record (EHR) environment.

summary: Strong strategies don't guarantee strong results. Many healthcare organizations struggle not because the strategy is wrong, but because they overlook the work required to put it into action.

title: Mainstreaming alternatives: The rise of alternative property sectors
summary: Commercial real estate investment has undergone a structural shift, with a growing share of allocations expanding beyond traditional core property sectors into alternative property sectors. While conventional property types continue to play a major role in real estate investment portfolios, changing economic conditions, demographic shifts, and evolving risk and return expectations have directed more capital to alternative real estate.

title: AI Applied: Get more value from ERP and legacy systems
summary: For many organizations, the first challenge in using AI for digital transformation is getting the right information out of the systems they already use. title: Medicare geographic reclassification can help hospitals improve reimbursement
summary: Medicare geographic reclassification is much more than a regulatory or administrative exercise. The Medicare geographic reclassification process is a strategic financial tool that can improve a hospital's long-term financial sustainability and help ensure Medicare payments accurately reflect the labor costs incurred to deliver patient care.

summary: Texas has joined a select list of states that offers a refundable research and development (R&D) tax credit , and this new credit has relatively few restrictions and limitations.

summary: Becoming a public company is no longer a singular event. It’s the beginning of a fundamentally different operating model, as detailed in Part I of this article series, IPO readiness is no longer enough .

summary: Healthcare has never shrugged off the importance of developing its people. title: CY 2027 OPPS proposed rule: 11 key changes to prepare for
summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has released the Calendar Year (CY) 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Proposed Rule, introducing several significant policy and payment changes that could materially affect hospital outpatient reimbursement, operational strategy, and long-term planning.

title: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) laws: What businesses need to know
summary: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is rapidly reshaping how companies manage packaging in the United States. Rather than placing the financial responsibility for collecting and recycling packaging on municipalities and taxpayers, EPR laws require producers to help fund and support these systems.

title: Beyond the myth: Why better patient access doesn’t mean burned-out doctors
summary: The reflex inside most health systems is to treat patient access and physician wellness as competing priorities. Push for more visits and you burn out the clinicians delivering them. Protect the clinicians and you accept the access constraints that come with the protection.

title: The coordination challenge behind healthcare strategy execution
summary: A large-scale strategic initiative at a regional health system was 12 months in. The scope was substantial—a dozen hospitals, several major service lines, multiple administrative and support functions, a set of interlocking initiatives that had to move roughly together to work.

title: Why access problems don't require a bigger checkbook in healthcare
summary: The first article of this series, Mission critical: Why patient access underpins your entire strategic plan, argued that access is the strategic capability that growth, risk, and affordability all depend on, and for many organizations, access has quietly become a single point of failure in the strategic plan. Once an executive team accepts that framing, the next question is the practical one: what do we do?

title: Four foundational questions for Tribal health leadership
summary: Tribal health leaders are navigating one of the most complex operating environments in American healthcare. Chronic disease burdens that exceed national averages by wide margins. Workforce shortages that outpace those of the broader health system. Communities whose health, history, and sovereignty call for a model of care built with intent, not one adapted from a generic template.
